heard: An asteroid sample was so huge it jammed its own lid. In October 2020, NASA's OSIRIS-Rx probe touched down on asteroid Bennu to collect a surface sample. A burst of nitrogen gas stirred up material, but the probe scooped up way too much. Large rocks jammed the collector's mylar lid open, letting precious asteroid dust drift away into space. Fearing more loss, mission controllers canceled a planned weighing spin and rushed to secure the harvest. On October 27, they successfully stowed the leaking sampler head inside the return capsule. Despite the leak, they recovered 121.6 grams over double the original mission goal. This record-shattering haul nearly caused total mission failure.
